fields.Summary: The Ann Marie Guenther Memorial Scholarship is provided by her loving husband Mark. Mark recognizes that education has the possibility to opens doors and create brighter futures. He intends to carry forth this outlook and also honor the passion Ann had for living life to the fullest through this memorial scholarship. The scholarship is open to high school seniors enrolled at Whitefish High School or Whitefish Independent High School who aspire to pursue higher education in a 2-year ($5K available) or 4-year (up to $10K available) college or university (12 credit minimum per semester). Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/10.

fields.Summary: The LeRoy W. Homer Jr. Foundation empowers future aviators to pursue their dreams of flight, honoring LeRoy’s legacy. The foundation builds a community of pilots embodying values of leadership, excellence, and service.

This is an automatic, merit-based scholarship for Montana freshmen demonstrating academic promise based on their cumulative high school GPA. Award amounts vary based on GPA, ranging from $1,000 to $4,000 per year, and are renewable for four years for tuition only. Students are automatically considered upon submitting an application for admission with a self-reported GPA.
This scholarship is automatically considered for new students pursuing their first bachelor's degree when they apply for admission to the University of Montana.

The Pell Promise for Montana Students is a financial aid initiative by Carroll College for Montana residents who are Federal Pell Grant recipients. It provides significant financial assistance, covering tuition, to eligible students who maintain a 3.0 GPA, reside on-campus, and accept a federal Stafford loan. It aims to enhance accessibility and affordability for under-served Montanans pursuing a Catholic, liberal arts education.

This scholarship awards $2,500 to a student pursuing an education in any skilled trade. Applicants must be US citizens or have a student visa, be a high school graduate or GED recipient, and be enrolled or plan to enroll full-time in a vocational/technical school or 2-year college for the fall 2025 semester, planning to acquire certification or degree in a skilled trade program. A GPA of 3.0 or higher is required.

fields.Summary: $1000 Scholarship will be awarded to one qualifying student from each of the following High Schools: Whitefish, Eureka, Bigfork, Columbia Falls, Glacier High and Flathead High, School Graduate; financial need and extracurricular/ community involvement in addition to higher-education plans are assessed; Application to be mailed to: Don K Whitefish, PO BOX 1178, Whitefish, MT 59937

CARD will award five, one-time, $2,000 scholarships for Montana seniors graduating high school in 2026 who come up with a design and write a brief paragraph (250 words maximum explaining the design) to create posters, T-shirts, stickers or decals, coasters, etc., dedicated to the question: What does “Alcohol Responsibility Matters” mean to you and your community? To qualify, high school seniors must be in good academic standing with their current institution of learning. If chosen, the funds will then be deposited with their school/apprentice program/certificate institute of higher learning. Applications (online or mailed) must be received by midnight Jan 25th 2026.
Include transcript, senior resume and answer 2 brief essays: 1) Please explain your financial needs 2) Brief statement on education and career goals. Submit to Mrs. Jones by end of day 4/15.

Black Mountain Software will be awarding two $1,000.00 scholarships to graduating seniors in Montana. Any Montana high school senior graduating in 2026 may apply if he or she will be attending an accredited institution of higher education. These accredited institutions include trade schools, technical schools, colleges or universities. The applicant’s field of study may be any field that they want to pursue. Applications and essays must be submitted electronically to Black Mountain Software. Please see the scholarship application for instructions for completing the application form and requirements for the essay. All submissions must be received before midnight on or before February 26th, 2026. Essay Question: If you were given a team of developers to build one new piece of software (an app, a program, a game) that would make the world a more joyful, curious, or connected place, what would it be and why? Describe its core function and the problem it solves for its users. The essay is limited to 2000 characters (300-350 words) or less.
Checklist to be completed and submitted

• Be a Clearwater Credit Union member for at least six months.
• Be a 2026 graduating high school senior OR a post-high school adult learner entering or enrolled in college.
• Have at least one transaction on any Clearwater deposit account within the last 60 days.
• Complete an online Financial Wellness Checkup in Clearwater’s online Financial Education Center by March 31, 2026, at 11:59pm.
• Check-up results are for informational purposes only and do NOT factor into scholarship consideration.
• Complete an online scholarship application by March 31, 2026, at 11:59pm.

A student can apply; in addition a member of the Whitefish community can nominate them. This scholarship is available to graduating seniors of Whitefish High School or Whitefish Independent High School who have experienced hardships, challenges due to disability, or discrimination in some way including but not limited to: economically (low-income), marginalized racially/ethnically, etc.  Paper applications to Mrs. Jones by 4/4.

Eligibility: Open to high school seniors enrolled at Whitefish High School who aspire to pursue further education in a 4-year, 2-year, or technical school within Montana. • Application Requirements: Interested students must submit the application form along with an essay addressing the provided prompt. Essays should be kept under 500 words. • No Minimum GPA Requirement: We believe in the potential of every student and encourage all eligible candidates to apply. Submit to Mrs. Jones by end of 4/11.

The Herriges Family Memorial Scholarship was established in memory of Nicholas and Anastasia Herriges by their children, all of whom were educated in the Whitefish schools. Grades, employment, extracurricular activities, community service and financial need are considered. Return applications to Mrs. Jones by: 4/20/26.

rows.source_name: Horatio Alger Association - Career & Technical Candidates

fields.Name of Scholarship: Horatio Alger Association - Career & Technical Candidates
fields.Summary: While most other scholarships focus exclusively on academic achievement or leadership potential, Horatio Alger Scholarships are also intended for promising students who have critical financial need ($100,000 or lower adjusted gross family income is required), demonstrate integrity and perseverance in overcoming adversity, and are determined to succeed. NOTE: By filling out one application, you will be considered for all scholarships for which you are eligible (but you will need to know WHICH scholarships you are interested in and select them from a list within your application)

Please attach a short, typed, essay (500 word maximum), explaining how this scholarship will help you “Reach Your Peak”.  You can return the completed applications to  Ms. Jones, your High School Career Guidance Counselor no later than April 1, 2026.

rows.source_name: Whitefish Lake Institute Ripple Effect Scholarship

fields.Name of Scholarship: Whitefish Lake Institute Ripple Effect Scholarship
fields.Summary: This scholarship is available to any Whitefish High School senior who is entering a four year university with plans to major in an environmental science field. Eligible majors include; environmental science/studies, environmental engineering, biology, and sustainability. Other majors will be considered if they demonstrate a link to an environmental emphasis. A brief essay also needs to be included (300-500 words) describing your “watershed ethic.” In short, what is your philosophy regarding human activities that affect water quality in the Whitefish Lake Watershed? How does your watershed ethic make you a good steward of water resources in the Whitefish Lake Watershed? Paper applications to be mailed to: Whitefish Lake Institute, Ripple Effect Applications 550 E. 1st St. #103 Whitefish, MT 59937 or emailed to: Info@whitefishlake.org // Subject: Ripple Effect Application

fields.Name of Scholarship: VFW Voices of Democracy - Patriotic Audio Essay “How Are You Showing Patriotism And Support For Our Country?”
fields.Summary: All entries must start with the local VFW post. Contact the Whitefish VFW to see about participating. Record your original 3-5 minute (+ or – 5 second max.) audio essay on a flash drive, or other electronic device. Hearing/speech impaired students should email the Voice of Democracy National Office at youth scholarships@vfw.org for special instructions. No music, singing, poetry or sound effects are allowed. The body of the essay must not identify you in any way, (including, but not limited to your name, school, city, state, race, or national origin) although the recording & typed essay should be labeled with your name, to show ownership. All entries competing at the local Post level must be in the hands of that VFW Post by midnight, Oct. 31, 2025.  Originality is worth 35 points (treatment of the theme should show imagination and human interest), Content is worth 30 points (clearly express your ideas in an organized manner. Fully develop your theme and use transitions to move smoothly from one idea to another), Delivery is worth 35 points (speak in a clear and credible manner). Read application for further details. You will submit the recording, typed essay and this completed entry form to: Dustin Wegner, Commander     20 Baker Ave., Whitefish, MT  59937 (you can mail or drop off in person). Call Dustin Wegner with questions: 406.654.4020

You do NOT need to be related to the Elks organization to apply! Students judged on scholarship and leadership. They are interested in students who are passionate about making a positive IMPACT on society. You do not have to be a member (or the dependent of a member) of the Elks. You will fill out online brief information about academic and leadership experience, in addition to providing a resume and counselor recommendation form. You will also answer the following essay question: Using one of the leadership roles or extracurricular activities you prioritized as being important to you, describe what impact the experience had on you, what you contributed, what you learned about yourself, and how it has influenced your plans for the future. (500 word max). WHen completing your online application, list KALISPELL POST code for sponsoring chapter (this has been confirmed with the State Scholarship Chair). Per State Scholarship Chair, VOLUNTEERISM is key to highlight. Questions? Contact: Dan Riddle 406-204-3054 dannyriddle406@yahoo.com

Senior, 3.75 GPA, Family gross income of less than $95,000. The application is online and via using the Common App. You will complete the Common App general requirements, which include things like your contact information, the school you attend and your grades, and your activities and honors. You will also invite your school counselor and two teachers to submit recommendations through the Common App. Once you have created a Common App, add the Jack Kent Cooke Foundation as one of your “schools” to access the application questions that are specific to the College Scholarship Program. These will include: Eligibility, Several short essays, Extracurricular activities and honors, Intended major, Financial information, including the last three years’ Adjusted Gross Income (AGI) for your household. Candidates are reviewed and selected based on leadership, academic ability and achievement, persistence, and unmet financial need.

These scholarships are offered to help defray costs of education (e.g., flight instruction, aircraft airframe and powerplant (A&P) mechanic school, etc.). Recipients will be announced in January 2026. Note special instructions for HOW to submit your application (they are very specific and will determine whether your application is viewed as "complete" by the organization)!

This year, we are awarding $2 million in scholarships to 600 students. Each year, scholarship recipients are selected based on their demonstration of the four pillars of NHS: Scholarship, Service, Leadership, and Character. Senior in NHS, NHS student account holder, attending an accredited college/university in the U.S. In the application process you will need to provide detailed information about activities and experiences related to scholarship, service, leadership, and character. You will also need to request an Adviser Certification from your NHS Adviser (acts as a short recommendation form and confirms the applicant is currently in good standing with a local NHS chapter. Request a Recommendation from one non-adviser, non-family member adult who can speak to the applicant’s commitment to the pillars of NHS. The recommendation must be completed in the application portal and no external documents or communications will be accepted.

The Hagan Scholarship is a nationwide need-based merit scholarship, designed to provide recipients with the opportunity to graduate college debt-free. Applicants must attend a traditional public high school governed by a school district. Free workshops, Free Schwab Brokerage Accounts and Free Study Abroad provide recipients with a practical understanding of important life skills not typically covered in the school curriculum. (Hagan Scholarship Brochure). Applicant’s Adjusted Gross Household Income reported for 2023 Federal Income Tax Purposes must not have exceeded $100,000. “Household Income” is defined as the total income received by all members of a household living under the same roof. Applicants must show evidence they will be working 240 hours from January 1, 2026 to September 1, 2026 (they understand that most recipients work during the summer months. Work can be part-time during their senior year in high school or full-time during the summer or a combination of the two. They are looking for "students willing to contribute toward their educational expenses."

Each year, the U.S. Junior Chamber International (JCI) Senate Foundation grants $1,500 scholarships to graduating high school seniors who plan to continue their education at accredited post-secondary colleges and universities. NOTE: there is a different application form for those applying to an Undergraduate vs. Vocational school! Application for Either postmarked BEFORE the 17th to: Janet Prescott 1060 Weaver Road Belgrade, MT 59714 Need to submit *UP TO* 500 word personal statement in addition for *UP TO* 3 letters of recommendation. See application for additional materials. Contact Nancy Salopek via email at scholarship@usjcisenate.org with questions!
